stimuli.title: Eight boxes labelled Deepa, Nisha, Kiran, Charu, Bina, Riya, Gita, Ovi are stacked one above another. Position 1 is at the bottom and position 8 at the top.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Kiran occupies position 2 from the bottom.
• Exactly 3 boxes are between Nisha and Gita.
• Exactly 2 boxes are between Nisha and Charu.
• Deepa and Ovi are adjacent boxes.
• Exactly 2 boxes are between Nisha and Ovi.
• Exactly 1 box is between Bina and Ovi.

• The floor numbers of Gita and Sana differ by 2.

• Farah and Kiran occupy flats with the same letter on different floors.

• Gita and Farah live on the same floor.
• The floor numbers of Gita and Nisha differ by 1.

stimuli.title: Aditi, Hema, Uma, Deepa, Pia, Gita, Charu, Jaya attend interviews, one per slot, on 7 and 21 March, April, May and June. Slots run in chronological order.

Use all the following clues:

questions.stem:
Statements: Some cheques are coins. All coins are files. No files is a deposits.
Conclusions:
I. Some cheques are files.
II. Some coins are deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few cheques are coins. All coins are files. No files is a deposits.
Conclusions:
I. Some cheques are not coins.
II. No coins is a deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few cheques are coins. Some coins are files. All files are deposits.
Conclusions:
I. All cheques are deposits.
II. No coins is a deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No cheques is a coins. Some coins are files. All files are deposits.
Conclusions:
I. All cheques are deposits.
II. Some deposits are coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: R > W < Q > S < X.
Conclusions: I. Q ≥ W   II. Q ≥ X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. X > V   II. Q ≤ V.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
banking access digital = su ze ni
banking growth credit = re su vo
access growth secure = lu re ze
digital credit secure = vo ni lu
banking access secure = su ze lu
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: re. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: banking = su, access = ze, digital = ni, growth = re, credit = vo, secure = lu.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 94 km south, turns right and walks 192 km, then turns right and walks 14 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 208. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 80 km along the initial direction and 192 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(80² + 192²) = 208 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 110 km south, turns right and walks 216 km, then turns right and walks 20 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 234. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 90 km along the initial direction and 216 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(90² + 216²) = 234 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 32 km north, turns right and walks 24 km, then turns right and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 26. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 10 km along the initial direction and 24 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(10² + 24²) = 26 km.

questions.stem: G is the mother of D. H is the son of D. E is the father of D. How is H related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. E is a parent of D, and H is D’s son. Hence H is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of A. A is the mother of C. G is the father of E and A. How is E related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of C’s mother A. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of C. C is the father of H. B is the son of H. A is the sister of C. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of H, and H is B’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 63 candidates, a candidate is 8th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 53. New front rank = 8+3 = 11. Back rank = 63 − 11 + 1 = 53.

questions.stem: In a queue of 44 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 22. New front rank = 19+4 = 23. Back rank = 44 − 23 + 1 = 22.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1100. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 1527.78. Selling price = 1100 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.9 = 1527.78.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 13.33. Use 60 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 60 − 4×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 117 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 11 km/h and stream speed is 2 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹16000 for 12 months. B invests ₹64000 for 5 months. Total profit is ₹96000. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 60000. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 20. B’s share = total × 20/(32) = 60000.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹28000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 280. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 28000 × (10/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 45 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 9. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 9.

questions.stem: The average of 17 numbers is 52. One number, 64, is replaced and the average rises by 8. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 200. Total increases by 17 × 8. New number = 64 + 136.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 8 years, their combined age will be 96 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 16 = 96; x = 20, so father = 60.

questions.stem: A train of length 150 m crosses a 100 m platform at 79.2 km/h. Find crossing time in seconds (to two decimals).
A village has 3500 registered customers. This increases by 25% in year 1 and decreases by 30% in year 2. What is the final number? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 3062.5. Apply successive factors: 3500 × 125/100 × 70/100.
